prerequisites: Prior knowledge in Physics, Mechanics, and Mathematics
Elasticity and Strength of Materials I and II

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and ability for the calculation and design of structures and industrial constructions.
Knowledge and abilities to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, and is typically found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated through the development and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, that enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, abilities and skills in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.

syllabus_topics: Generalities. Concept of Structure. Calculation in the general design process. Typology.
Fundamental relationships. Equilibrium. Compatibility. Constitutive law.
Work, strain energy and their complements
Integral formulation of the boundary value problem. Principle of virtual work
Applications of the principle of virtual work. Application of the P.V.W. in articulated node structures. Application of the P.V.W. in general bar structures.
Resolution methods. Node method. Cremona. Sections.
Release of constraints. Choice of hyperstatic unknowns.
Degrees of freedom. Definitions, simplifications and hypotheses.
Constitutive relationships of the prismatic bar
Matrix formulation of the Stiffness Method
Analysis methods. Generalization of bifurcation approaches.
Step-by-step methods for bar structure calculation.
teaching_methods: Theoretical study and analysis of solved examples
Voluntary complementary activities (study and application of Finite Element Method)
assessment_rules: The final grade is the greater of two options: either 80% of the Face-to-face Exam grade plus 20% of the Continuous Assessment Tests (PEC) grade, or solely the Face-to-face Exam grade. The combined formula applies only if the Face-to-face Exam grade is at least 4 out of 10 and a minimum of 30% of the score is achieved in each exam question. PECs are optional; if completed in their entirety, they account for 20% of the final grade, but will never reduce the Face-to-face Exam score. PECs are considered for ordinary and extraordinary calls but are not carried over to subsequent years.
